TwistedFate.phase: Late game, Vex R Shadow Surge becomes powerful for chained engages through its kill reset, but don’t rush in if the enemy is grouped and won’t give you an angle for your ultimate.
TwistedFate.teamfight: Don’t engage first. If you see Twisted Fate moving with R Destiny and he’s in range, interrupt him with a basic ability empowered by Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear. Then catch the backline with Vex E Looming Darkness, and engage with Vex R Shadow Surge once Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s gold card has been used and a finish is certain.
TwistedFate.watch: When Twisted Fate W Pick a Card has locked in a gold card, one basic attack will stun you, so stay outside his attack range.

Veigar.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Veigar’s magic damage. Choose Mercury’s Treads and prioritize magic resistance.
Veigar.combo: Cast Vex E Looming Darkness from range to slow Veigar, then hit him with Vex Q Mistral Bolt; if the mark remains, weave in one basic attack. If Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear is ready, apply it to Veigar with the longer-range Q or wider-area E.
Veigar.escape: Engage after Veigar E Event Horizon is down. Veigar has no skill to create distance, so hit him with Vex R Shadow Surge and dash in when you can finish him. If you’re trapped by E, don’t blindly cross its edge; use R when you escape.
Veigar.fight: Poke Veigar with Vex Q Mistral Bolt when he steps up to last-hit minions. In trades, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness before landing Q, and use Vex W Personal Space’s shield when Veigar’s burst damage hits.
Veigar.laning: Veigar Q Baleful Strike only pierces the first two units it hits, so stand behind minions to avoid taking unnecessary damage.
Veigar.phase: In the late game, Veigar’s stacking growth makes the matchup less favorable as time goes on, so check his position and whether Veigar E Event Horizon has been used before fighting over objectives.
Veigar.teamfight: Don’t dash in first. When the enemy engages, interrupt them with Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear, then catch the backline with Vex E Looming Darkness. Check whether Veigar E Event Horizon has been used, and use Vex R Shadow Surge on a target you can certainly kill once their formation is broken, aiming for the reset.
Veigar.watch: Veigar E Event Horizon stuns you if you cross its edge, so if you’re trapped, move around inside and wait for it to disappear instead of running into the edge. Dodge Veigar W Dark Matter to the side after watching its ground indicator, and when health falls below half, get out of range of Veigar R Primordial Burst, which deals more damage based on missing health.

Vladimir.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads. Vladimir’s main damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance, and add Grievous Wounds if the duel runs long.
Vladimir.combo: After Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness and fire Vex Q Mistral Bolt. If the Gloom mark remains, consume it with one basic attack. Chain Vex R Shadow Surge when you can finish Vladimir and Vex W Personal Space will still be available for after the dash.
Vladimir.escape: Right after Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends is your chance to close the gap with Vex R Shadow Surge. Vladimir’s movement speed slows while charging Vladimir E Tides of Blood, so you can also dodge the wave and close the gap during its charge.
Vladimir.fight: Poke Vladimir with Vex Q Mistral Bolt when he steps up to last-hit minions. Once Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness and hit him with Vex Q Mistral Bolt. Use Vex W Personal Space’s shield when Vladimir’s damage hits.
Vladimir.laning: Save Vex E Looming Darkness for trades, and don’t spend Vex P Doom ’n Gloom on clearing minions when it’s active.
Vladimir.phase: Late game, look for a kill reset with Vex R Shadow Surge, but don’t dive first if the enemy is grouped and gives you no angle to engage.
Vladimir.teamfight: Don’t group up where multiple people can be hit by Vladimir R Hemoplague; if you’re infected, re-engage after its effect ends. Look for a chance to catch the enemy backline with Vex E Looming Darkness instead of engaging first. When Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down and a finish is certain, engage with Vex R Shadow Surge and aim for the reset.
Vladimir.watch: Vladimir Q Transfusion provides healing, movement speed, and an empowered ability, so keep your distance when he approaches with an empowered Q Transfusion. When he charges Vladimir E Tides of Blood, put minions between you or move out of range, and save Vex’s decisive abilities while Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is available. Vladimir R Hemoplague increases the damage you take, so step back until its effect ends if you’re infected.

Xerath.build: Withstand the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads. Xerath’s main damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance.
Xerath.combo: For a short trade, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness, then hit him with Vex Q Mistral Bolt; if the Gloom mark remains, consume it with a basic attack. To engage, hit him with Vex R Shadow Surge and recast it to dash in, then use Vex E Looming Darkness and Vex W Personal Space after landing.
Xerath.escape: Xerath has no mobility spell, so engage with Vex R Shadow Surge right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Xerath can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so it’s a chance to dodge or engage on his position.
Xerath.fight: The moment after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down is your chance to fight. Hit him with Vex R Shadow Surge to close the gap, but check that Vex W Personal Space is still available to deal with what comes after the dash.
Xerath.laning: Farm early while avoiding Xerath’s heavy damage, and poke with Vex Q Mistral Bolt when he steps up to last-hit minions. Save Vex E Looming Darkness for trades, and when Xerath has spent a lot of mana, push the lane and call your jungler.
Xerath.teamfight: Look for a chance to catch the enemy backline with Vex E Looming Darkness instead of engaging first. Once Xerath E Shocking Orb is down and his formation is broken, engage with Vex R Shadow Surge when a finish is certain and aim for the reset.
Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse pierces minions, so when you see him charging, dodge widely to the side. Be especially careful if you’re stunned by Xerath E Shocking Orb, since you can easily take follow-up damage, and activate Vex W Personal Space’s shield when damage hits.

Yasuo.build: Buy Cloth Armor first in the early game and choose Plated Steelcaps. Yasuo’s main damage is physical and Vex has low armor, so prioritize armor. If the enemy team has several diving assassins, prioritize Zhonya’s Hourglass ahead of other damage items so you can survive after engaging with Vex R Shadow Surge.
Yasuo.combo: Remove Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield first, then slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness and fire Vex Q Mistral Bolt at the slowed Yasuo. If Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s mark remains, consume it with one basic attack and back off. If Yasuo E Sweeping Blade has already brought him close, put the saved fear on Vex W Personal Space to stop the dash and gain a shield.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo Q Steel Tempest fires its tornado and before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back are your chances to attack. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t engage with Vex R Shadow Surge just because he used it once. Stop his engage with fear or apply crowd control, and dash in when you can finish a target marked by R.
Yasuo.fight: First remove Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield with light poke, then trade seriously. When Yasuo E Sweeping Blade dashes in, save Vex P Doom ’n Gloom and put the fear on a basic ability to stop his dash and counterattack. Right after Yasuo Q Steel Tempest fires its tornado, he briefly has no way to knock you up, so look for a chance to attack.
Yasuo.laning: Use Vex Q Mistral Bolt to farm and poke, adding Q when Yasuo steps up to last-hit minions. Save Vex E Looming Darkness for trades, and don’t spend Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear on clearing minions.
Yasuo.phase: Late game, chained engages are powerful because R resets on kills, but wait for a chance to finish a target if the enemy groups up and gives you no angle for R.
Yasuo.teamfight: In team fights, don’t engage first. Respond when Yasuo engages with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade or Yasuo R Last Breath by using a basic ability empowered by Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear. Then catch the enemy backline with Vex E Looming Darkness. Once the enemy formation is broken, use Vex R Shadow Surge on a target you can certainly kill and aim for the reset.
Yasuo.watch: Yasuo Q Steel Tempest has a narrow hitbox, so when he approaches, leave his line and dodge to the side. After he hits Q twice, his next Q becomes a tornado that knocks you up, so watch for its sound and visual effects and dodge early. Save projectile Vex R Shadow Surge while Yasuo W Wind Wall is up; look for an angle around the wall or wait for it to disappear.

Yone.build: Yone deals both physical and magic damage, so don’t focus on only one type of resistance. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that greatly increase health alone. If the enemy team has several diving assassins, prioritize Zhonya’s Hourglass ahead of damage items so you can survive after engaging with Vex R Shadow Surge.
Yone.combo: For a safe trade, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness, then hit him with Vex Q Mistral Bolt; if the mark remains, weave in one basic attack. If Yone dashes in, interrupt his engage with a basic ability empowered by the Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear you saved. If he’s already close, you can fear him while gaining a shield with Vex W Personal Space.
Yone.escape: If only Yone Q Mortal Steel is down, Yone can still escape with Yone E Soul Unbound or Yone R Fate Sealed, so don’t rush the engage. In particular, look for a chance before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back, and use Vex R Shadow Surge to close the gap during a window when his other mobility and crowd control are down. Before using R to engage, check that Vex W Personal Space and Flash are available.
Yone.fight: When Yone’s tornado is ready, don’t close the gap first. When he engages, interrupt his dash with Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear and counterattack. If Yone R Fate Sealed is still down, look for a chance to close the gap with Vex R Shadow Surge. But if Yone still has another mobility spell, don’t engage just because one ability is down.
Yone.laning: Keep your distance when Yone prepares a tornado with Yone Q Mortal Steel, and don’t use Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear to clear minions. Save Vex E Looming Darkness for fights.
Yone.phase: Late game, look for chained engages through Vex R Shadow Surge’s reset after a kill, but don’t force it if the enemy groups up and gives you no angle for R.
Yone.teamfight: Don’t engage first. Interrupt Yone’s engages with Yone Q Mortal Steel, Yone E Soul Unbound, or Yone R Fate Sealed using Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear. Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield doesn’t grow, and check that you aren’t alone at the very back of your formation in case of Yone R Fate Sealed. After stopping his engage, catch the backline with Vex E Looming Darkness, then use Vex R Shadow Surge on a target you can certainly kill and aim for the reset.
Yone.watch: When Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions to prepare a tornado, stay out of range and wait for the stacks to disappear. Save Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear for when Yone engages with Yone E Soul Unbound or uses Yone R Fate Sealed, then interrupt his engage with a basic ability.

Zed.build: Withstand the early game with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps. Zed’s main damage is physical and Vex has low armor, so prioritize armor. If the enemy team has several diving assassins, prioritize Zhonya’s Hourglass ahead of other damage items so you can survive after engaging with Vex R Shadow Surge.
Zed.combo: For a basic trade, slow him with Vex E Looming Darkness and hit him with Vex Q Mistral Bolt; if the Gloom mark remains, weave in one basic attack. If Zed is already close, put Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear on Vex W Personal Space to gain a shield as you respond. If you engage with Vex R Shadow Surge on a target you can finish, use Vex E Looming Darkness and Vex W Personal Space immediately after landing.
Zed.escape: Look for an opening after Zed W Living Shadow disappears or after Zed has already changed position. Don’t engage immediately just because Zed W Living Shadow is down; also check whether Zed R Death Mark is still down. Close the gap with Vex R Shadow Surge during that window, but engage only when you can finish the target.
Zed.fight: Wait for Zed to engage and preserve Vex P Doom ’n Gloom; when he comes in, interrupt him with a basic ability empowered by fear, then counterattack. The chance to trade is after Zed W Living Shadow disappears or after Zed has already changed position. When engaging with Vex R Shadow Surge, choose a target you can finish and check that Vex W Personal Space and Flash are available.
Zed.laning: Use Vex Q Mistral Bolt to farm and poke, adding poke when Zed steps up to last-hit minions. Save Vex E Looming Darkness for fights, and if Zed closes in, respond with Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear and Vex W Personal Space’s shield. If you’ve spent the fear on minions, retreat behind them while Zed can easily close in.
Zed.phase: Late game, group with your allies to reduce the number of targets Zed can pick off alone, and look for a target Vex can finish to get a reset with Vex R Shadow Surge.
Zed.teamfight: Don’t engage first. When Zed engages with Zed W Living Shadow or Zed R Death Mark, interrupt him with a basic ability empowered by Vex P Doom ’n Gloom’s fear. Then catch the enemy backline with Vex E Looming Darkness. Once the enemy formation is broken and a finish is certain, engage with Vex R Shadow Surge and aim for the reset.
Zed.watch: When Zed approaches with Zed W Living Shadow and Zed R Death Mark, save Vex P Doom ’n Gloom to interrupt his dash and fear him. Watch the shadow’s position and dodge outside the range of Zed E Shadow Slash’s slow.

Zoe.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zoe deals mostly magic damage, and Vex has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. However, resistance cannot block the true damage from Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble, so dodging the bubble comes first.
Zoe.combo: A basic trade goes: slow with Vex E Looming Darkness, hit Vex Q Mistral Bolt, then add one basic attack if Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s mark remains. If you know where Zoe R Portal Jump will return her, hit that spot with Vex E Looming Darkness and continue with follow-up attacks. If Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s fear is ready, use a basic ability to fear Zoe just as she throws Zoe Q Paddle Star! to set up its angle, disrupting her re-aim.
Zoe.escape: The moment after Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble goes down is your chance to engage with Vex R Shadow Surge. Zoe R Portal Jump returns her to its starting point after she moves, so target that return location or close the distance while Zoe R Portal Jump is down.
Zoe.fight: When Zoe steps up to last-hit a minion, chip away at her health with Vex Q Mistral Bolt. When Zoe uses R Portal Jump, aim at the spot where she will return to, then land Vex E Looming Darkness’s slow and follow-up attacks. Before engaging with Vex R Shadow Surge, check whether Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down.
Zoe.laning: Save Vex E Looming Darkness for a fight, and don’t spend Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s fear on clearing minions when it is active. Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble leaves a trap where it misses, so move around that spot.
Zoe.phase: In the late game, Vex R Shadow Surge is powerful for chaining engages when a kill resets it, but loses impact if the enemy team groups up and gives you no opening to engage.
Zoe.teamfight: Instead of engaging first, respond when Zoe uses Zoe R Portal Jump with a basic ability carrying Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s fear. Then use Vex E Looming Darkness to lock down the enemy backline, and engage with Vex R Shadow Surge when Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down and you can finish the target off. Before engaging, check that Vex W Personal Space and Flash are available.
Zoe.watch: Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble puts you to sleep after a short delay if it hits, leaving you open to heavy follow-up damage. Dodge the bubble when you see it. If it hits, move behind a wall or an ally before the sleep triggers to get out of Zoe Q Paddle Star!’s angle and range. A bubble that misses still leaves a trap, so watch narrow paths without vision and brush entrances.
